title: STATIC FOX gaming channel pack: pull six peak frames from mixed-light captures to one house grade, author an A/B hero-thumbnail SET, prep two brand graphics into reusable overlays, and cut three same-length reframes
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com comedy-gameplay YouTube brief (creator supplies raw captures plus rough notes and custom graphics and wants an entertaining, fast-paced upload with reaction zooms, on-screen text call-outs and meme cutaways, a thumbnail, and a reusable project file). The literal asks in that brief — timeline trims to flagged timestamps, animated reaction zooms, motion-graphic text call-outs composited over the video, and on-video meme overlays — are all on the connector's NOT-AVAILABLE list (no trim-to-timestamp, no motion graphics, no compositing over video), so the job is honestly re-cast to the in-scope, connector-doable spine of a channel-launch graphics + reframe package while staying faithful to the same intent (a punchy, cohesive upload plus reusable overlay assets and a click-worthy thumbnail). The fictional channel STATIC FOX (a comedy-gaming persona), its fox-head emblem, its cartoon mascot, and the fictional unbranded game 'Ridgeline Tactics' are invented for this benchmark; no real game, studio, streamer, brand or trademark appears. ENRICHMENT (needed to make the chain concrete, failable and measurable): the creator captured the same 'Ridgeline Tactics' session across SIX short clips at different in-game times of day (dusk, dawn, night, overcast, golden-hour, blue-hour) so the raw footage does NOT match clip-to-clip; each clip frames the same weathered matte mid-grey concrete barrier lit by the scene, which is the honest neutralisation reference (the in-world equivalent of a grey card); the primary clip carries the creator's live comedic voice-over on its audio track. The six-clip time-of-day split, the in-scene grey concrete reference, the 2160p capture-card resolution, the two brand rasters (flat emblem vs photoreal mascot render), and the output dimensions are reasonable enrichment; nothing contradicts the source. Freelancer.com / YouTube / Shorts are platform names, not brands in the scene. NO invented capability: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no on-video overlays, no font design; video contributes only frame-pulls, same-length reframes, speech enhance and a content summary; every graphic is authored from the pulled stills or the supplied brand rasters.
one_line_ask: Take a comedy-gaming creator's six mixed-lighting 'Ridgeline Tactics' captures, pull the strongest frame from each and grade the six to ONE STATIC FOX house look (the in-scene grey concrete landing neutral at a common brightness and floor), author a genuine A/B hero-thumbnail SET in two different art directions, prep the two brand graphics each into its correct reuse form (a mark that stays razor-sharp at any size and a drop-anywhere transparent cut-out), clean the primary clip's commentary, and reframe it to three same-length platform cuts.
full_brief:
STATIC FOX is a comedy-gaming YouTube channel relaunching its look, and the raw footage is a mess of mismatched clips. What you're handed: six short 2160p screen-captures of the same 'Ridgeline Tactics' session, each grabbed at a different in-game time of day (dusk, dawn, night, overcast, golden-hour, blue-hour). Straight off the capture card they do NOT match each other — one runs magenta-warm, another cold-blue, another flat and grey, and they sit at different brightnesses. Every clip happens to frame the same weathered matte mid-grey concrete barrier, lit by the scene — the one dependable neutral-grey surface that shows up in all six. The primary dusk clip also carries the creator's live voice-over commentary. You also get two 'brand' graphics: a fox-head EMBLEM and a 3D MASCOT render (a cartoon fox in a bomber jacket).

What we need back, and the bar for each:

1) SIX matched chapter stills. Pull the single strongest, most readable frame out of each of the six clips (skip the dead-air walking frames — grab the peak comedic beat) and grade the six so the channel's community/chapter grid reads as ONE room: the grey concrete barrier must land truly neutral — no residual warm or cool cast — at ONE common brightness across all six, and the darkest shadows must floor at ONE common near-black that is deep but never crushed to pure black. The catch is that the six start from completely different lighting, so getting all six to sit together as one set — matched at that concrete and matched down in the shadows — is the whole job. We judge the grid as a WHOLE: six frames that each look fine on their own but don't read as the same room are exactly what we reject.

2) An A/B HERO-THUMBNAIL SET. From the best of the pulled frames, give us TWO thumbnails that are two genuinely DIFFERENT art directions we can split-test — not the same look twice. Direction A is loud clickbait energy: bright, punchy, high-contrast, warm and saturated. Direction B is a moody cinematic treatment: pulled-down and desaturated with cool teal shadows. Both 1280x720, both composed with the subject to one side so we can drop our own title text into the open space later (do NOT add text yourself).

3) Reusable brand overlays. Both brand graphics need prepping so we can reuse them everywhere. The EMBLEM is our channel mark — it rides as a small corner watermark on every video and blows up big on the end-card, so it has to stay pin-sharp at every size, from tiny bug to full-screen, with no soft edges or jaggies ever. The MASCOT we want to be able to drop onto anything — thumbnails, end-cards, panels — sitting cleanly on top of whatever is behind it, with none of its own background clinging to it. Prep each one into the form its job needs.

4) The upload cuts. Clean up the commentary on the primary clip so the voice is clear, and give us three platform reframes of that clip at the SAME length (no re-timing): the 16:9 master, a 9:16 vertical for Shorts, and a 1:1 square.

Along with the files, hand back a short sheet listing, per pulled still, the white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure and black-point you dialled, plus the two grades you chose for thumbnails A and B — so we can confirm the set really was matched to one target and the A/B pair are two directions, not one look nudged twice.

inputs.name: ridgeline_clip_01_dusk_primary.mp4

Player moves through a dusty unbranded industrial compound holding a rifle in first-person view; a large weathered MATTE MID-GREY CONCRETE BARRIER wall fills much of the left-middle of the frame, lit directly by the scene. Minimal clean HUD: a small crosshair dot, a plain light-grey ammo/health bar along the bottom, a minimap in the lower-left corner; NO readable or garbled text anywhere on screen, upper area kept as empty sky. DUSK lighting: a warm magenta-orange sky cast washing the whole scene warm. One clear comedic peak beat mid-clip (the player fumbles and trips over a crate) surrounded by calmer walking. Authentic flat in-game 3D-rendered game-capture footage, NOT live-action, NOT a photograph. Plain unbranded fictional military setting; NO real brand names, logos, trademarks, real game titles or weapon brands on the HUD, weapon, walls, crates or any surface. ~12s clip.
inputs.realism_notes: PRIMARY clip and the frame that establishes the house look. inputs.name: static_fox_mascot_render.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A photoreal 3D-rendered cartoon MASCOT character: a confident cartoon fox wearing a green bomber jacket and a headset, glossy stylised 3D shading with soft rim light, standing in a three-quarter pose. inputs.realism_notes: Photoreal shaded 3D render on a busy background — the REMOVE-BACKGROUND half of the triage: it must be isolated to a transparent cut-out with image_remove_background (semantic subject isolation), NOT vectorized. outputs.name: chapter_stills_matched_x6
outputs.spec: Six chapter/community stills, one peak frame pulled from each of the six clips (ridgeline_clip_01..06) and graded so the whole set reads as one room: the in-scene matte mid-grey concrete barrier reads visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance of each other) at ONE common brightness across all six, and the darkest shadows floor at ONE common near-black (deep, not clipped to 0, no channel crushed). Each frame's correction is DIFFERENT (warm dusk/golden cooled, cold dawn/night/blue-hour warmed, flat overcast given contrast). sRGB PNG at the native 3840x2160 pull resolution (downscale/no upscale). Acceptance: grey concrete neutral + common brightness + common black-floor across all six; the agent must REPORT per-still temperature/tint/exposure/black. DELIVERABLE 1.

outputs.name: thumbnail_A_high_energy_1280x720.png

Downscale of the 2160p pulled still, sRGB PNG. DELIVERABLE 2a.

outputs.name: thumbnail_B_cinematic_1280x720.png
outputs.spec: Hero thumbnail, art direction B ('moody cinematic'): from the SAME pulled frame as A, authored the opposite way — exposure pulled down, contrast shaped, saturation reduced, then a teal-shadow monochromatic duotone tint — a genuinely different look from A, not a variant of the same stack; cropped/resized to exactly 1280x720 with subject-to-one-side title space. sRGB PNG. DELIVERABLE 2b. A and B together are the A/B split-test SET.

outputs.name: static_fox_emblem.svg
outputs.spec: Crisp vector SVG of the flat two-colour fox-head emblem, produced by white drop-out to transparency, trim-to-bounds, then raster-to-vector trace of the prepared mark — sharp at any zoom for the watermark and end-card. DELIVERABLE 3.

outputs.name: static_fox_mascot_cutout.png
outputs.spec: The photoreal mascot render isolated onto a transparent background via semantic subject isolation (image_remove_background), busy arcade background removed, glossy fur/fabric edges preserved — a drop-anywhere overlay cut-out. outputs.name: master_16x9_enhanced.mp4
outputs.spec: The primary dusk clip reframed to a 1920x1080 16:9 master (same length as source, honest downscale from 2160p) with its voice-over commentary speech-enhanced for clarity. H.264/MP4. DELIVERABLE 5a.

outputs.name: shorts_9x16_1080x1920.mp4
outputs.spec: A 9:16 vertical Shorts reframe of the primary clip, 1080x1920, SAME length as the source (reframe only, no re-timing), honest downscale/crop of the 3840x2160 source (target height 1920 <= source 2160, no upscale). H.264/MP4. DELIVERABLE 5b.

outputs.name: square_1x1_1080x1080.mp4
outputs.spec: A 1:1 square reframe of the primary clip, 1080x1080, SAME length as the source (reframe only), honest downscale/crop of the 3840x2160 source. H.264/MP4. DELIVERABLE 5c.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the six pulled stills, the white-balance temperature/tint, exposure offset and black-point applied, plus the single common house-target brightness and black-floor all six were matched to; and the two DIVERGENT grade recipes chosen for thumbnails A and B. This is the acceptance artifact — it makes 'the set is matched to one target' and 'A/B are two real directions' checkable; the six corrections must be non-identical and A vs B must differ substantially. Applied-settings log, NOT a measurement (no read pixel values).

outputs.name: project_package
outputs.spec: A managed Creative Cloud project folder holding every source clip and brand raster plus every produced asset (six matched stills, A/B thumbnails, emblem SVG, mascot cut-out, three reframes, grade report) as the reusable 'project file' reference package.

connector_workflow.note: Create a managed Creative Cloud project folder ('StaticFox_Channel_Pack') to hold every source and produced asset — the reusable project-file package root. Plumbing, not counted as difficulty.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: ridgeline_clip_01_dusk_primary.mp4, ridgeline_clip_02_dawn.mp4, ridgeline_clip_03_night.mp4, ridgeline_clip_04_overcast.mp4, ridgeline_clip_05_golden.mp4, ridgeline_clip_06_bluehour.mp4, static_fox_emblem.png, static_fox_mascot_render.png
connector_workflow.note: Load the six mixed-lighting captures and the two brand rasters into the project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not the difficulty.

Summarise the primary dusk clip's content/structure (with its voice-over commentary) to locate the standout comedic beat and the readable stretches. Used as editorial steering for WHICH frame to pull as the hero and where each clip's peak sits — a content summary, not a beat/tempo profile. Async-widget.

Pull the single strongest, most readable frame from the dusk primary — the peak comedic beat, NOT a dead-air walking frame (a wrong pull yields a boring still that breaks both the matched set and the thumbnail). This 3840x2160 still is also the hero source for the A/B thumbnails. Decision step, guided by step 3. Async-widget.
Pull the peak frame from the dawn clip (the flinch beat), skipping the calmer walking. 3840x2160 still for the matched chapter set.
Pull the peak frame from the night clip (the walk-into-wall beat). 3840x2160 still for the matched chapter set.
Pull the peak frame from the overcast clip (the ledge face-plant). 3840x2160 still for the matched chapter set.
Pull the peak frame from the golden-hour clip (the early-celebration knockdown). 3840x2160 still for the matched chapter set.
Pull the peak frame from the blue-hour clip (the mistimed jump). 3840x2160 still for the matched chapter set.

ESTABLISH the STATIC FOX house look on the dusk frame and record it as the target the other five must hit. Using the scene-lit mid-grey concrete barrier as reference, COOL the temperature and set tint to drive that concrete to true neutral (kills the warm dusk cast), then build the house tonality with image_apply_adjustments primitives: set blacks so the darkest shadows floor at the house near-black (deep, not clipped), shape contrast/clarity for a punchy gamer look, hold highlights. Authored grade, NOT a preset, NOT auto-tone. The temp/tint/exposure/black chosen here DEFINE the common target. Agent reports them. DELIVERABLE 1 (frame 1).

Grade the dawn frame to the SAME target. It is COOL (pale blue), the OPPOSITE cast to the dusk hero, so WARM the temperature to neutralise the concrete and lift exposure toward the shared brightness, then seat the common black-floor and contrast. Correction sign flips vs frame 1 — copying frame 1's numbers is the trap. Report its distinct values. DELIVERABLE 1 (frame 2).

Grade the night frame to the common target — the strongest correction. Deep cold-blue and dark, so apply the largest warm shift and LIFT exposure to the shared brightness while holding the black-floor (charcoal shadows must not crush to pure 0). Report its distinct values. DELIVERABLE 1 (frame 3).

Grade the overcast frame to the common target — a RESTRAINT case. It is near-neutral but flat and muddy, so add CONTRAST and only a slight warm bias to land the concrete neutral at the shared brightness; over-warming a near-neutral frame tints it orange. Report its distinct values. DELIVERABLE 1 (frame 4).

Grade the golden-hour frame to the common target. Strong warm and BRIGHT, so COOL the temperature and pull exposure DOWN (opposite exposure direction to the night frame) while protecting the hot concrete highlights, then seat the common black-floor. Report its distinct values. DELIVERABLE 1 (frame 5).

Grade the blue-hour frame to the common target. Cold steel-blue and medium-dim, so warm the temperature (a different magnitude than the dawn/night frames), add midtone contrast, hold the blue out of the neutral concrete, and land the shared black-floor. Report its distinct values. Steps 10-15 are chapter_stills_matched_x6, each a DIFFERENT correction converging on one house target. DELIVERABLE 1 (frame 6).

A/B thumbnail, DIRECTION A ('loud clickbait energy') from the hero pulled frame: author bright and punchy — lift exposure, push contrast and vibrance/saturation, warm push — a deliberately LOUDER look than the editorial chapter grade (different purpose: stop the scroll). Built from the raw pull, not the house grade, so A and B are two independent directions. Authored from primitives, not a preset. Report the recipe.

Crop/resize direction A to exactly 1280x720 with the subject composed to one side so the creator can drop title text into the open space (no text added). onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'); downscale of the 2160p still, never enlarged. DELIVERABLE 2a.

A/B thumbnail, DIRECTION B ('moody cinematic') from the SAME hero pulled frame: the opposite move to A — pull exposure DOWN, shape contrast, REDUCE saturation for a restrained base. Distinct authored direction, not a tweak of A. Report the recipe.

Lay a teal-shadow monochromatic duotone tint over direction B for the cinematic look — a genuinely different treatment from A's loud warm push. Whole-image tint is the intended effect here (a full-frame thumbnail grade), not a masked recolor. Report the tint choice.

Crop/resize direction B to exactly 1280x720 with subject-to-one-side title space, matching A's framing intent but the opposite grade. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale only. DELIVERABLE 2b. Together with 2a this is the A/B split-test SET the agent OWNS.

TRIAGE, emblem half: drop the flat white field of the two-colour fox-head emblem to transparency — white drop-out, no reconstruction — as prep for tracing. (The emblem is the VECTORIZE target; the mascot render is NOT — see step 24.) Consumes the uploaded emblem.

Prep-before-trace: trim the transparent emblem to its own tight bounds (removes the now-transparent generous white margin) so the vectorize step spends its trace resolution on the mark, not empty canvas, and leaves no stray border path. Consumes step 21.

Vectorize the prepared flat two-colour emblem to crisp SVG paths for the watermark and end-card. Raster-to-vector trace of a prepared raster (flat mark, white knocked to transparency, cropped to bounds). Correct because the source is flat hard-edged 2-colour art. DELIVERABLE 3. Consumes step 22.

TRIAGE, mascot half: isolate the photoreal 3D mascot render onto a TRANSPARENT background via semantic subject isolation — the CORRECT treatment for a shaded photoreal render on a busy arcade scene. It is deliberately NOT vectorized: tracing a photoreal render returns a flat black silhouette (the wrong-treatment failure the brief warns of). Getting the emblem/mascot triage backwards is invisible until inspected. DELIVERABLE 4. Consumes the uploaded mascot.
Reframe the 2160p primary dusk clip to a 1920x1080 16:9 master — same length, honest downscale of existing pixels (1920<=3840, 1080<=2160, no upscale). The YouTube master frame. Async-widget.
Enhance the creator's voice-over commentary on the 16:9 master so the speech is clear over the game audio. Consumes step 25. DELIVERABLE 5a. Async-widget.

Reframe the 2160p primary clip to a 9:16 vertical 1080x1920 Shorts cut — SAME length (reframe only, no re-timing), honest crop/downscale from 3840x2160 (target height 1920 <= source 2160, so no upscale). Cut from the full-res source, not the 1080p master, to stay downscale-only. DELIVERABLE 5b. Async-widget.

Reframe the 2160p primary clip to a 1:1 square 1080x1080 cut — SAME length (reframe only), honest crop/downscale from the full-res source. DELIVERABLE 5c. Async-widget. The three reframes (5a/5b/5c) plus the six matched stills, A/B thumbnails, emblem SVG and mascot cut-out all live in the project_folder from step 1 as the reusable package.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining across four tributaries that converge on one channel package. SETUP: create_folder (1) -> asset_add_file (2, single batch upload of six clips + two brand rasters) -> media_summarize (3, content summary of the primary clip steering frame selection). FRAME-PULL + MATCHED-GRADE tributary (the human-hard core): video_render_frame x6 (4-9, one peak frame per clip, a selection decision each) fan into six per-still image_apply_adjustments grades (10-15) that each reason a DIFFERENT correction to ONE house target read off the scene-lit grey concrete — dusk establishes the target (10), dawn/night/blue-hour warm up (11,12,15), golden-hour cools + pulls down (14), overcast gets contrast + restraint (13) — producing chapter_stills_matched_x6. A/B THUMBNAIL tributary (the OWNED endpoint): the dusk raw pull (still_01) feeds TWO independent directions — A loud-clickbait via image_apply_adjustments (16) -> crop_and_resize 1280x720 (17); B moody-cinematic via image_apply_adjustments (18) -> image_apply_monochromatic_tint teal duotone (19) -> crop_and_resize 1280x720 (20) — two genuinely divergent grades, not one stack twice. BRAND-TRIAGE tributary: the flat emblem takes remove_background white drop-out (21) -> crop_to_bounds (22) -> vectorize (23) = SVG; the photoreal mascot takes remove_background subject-isolation (24) = transparent cut-out, deliberately NOT vectorized. VIDEO-CUT tributary: the primary clip is reframed to a 1920x1080 master (25) then speech-enhanced (26), and independently reframed from the full-res source to 9:16 (27) and 1:1 (28), all same-length. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; nothing is loaded twice. 28 calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools spanning asset/storage, video/media, photo/raster and vector groups.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the killed on-video-overlay version: 28 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across four connector groups (asset/storage, video/media, photo/raster, vector), with four dependent tributaries that converge on one reusable channel package. Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the six matched-still grades are NOT one recipe run six times — each is a per-frame WB/exposure/black delta whose SIGN and magnitude flip by the clip's in-game time of day (warm dusk/golden cooled and pulled down, cold dawn/night/blue-hour warmed and lifted, flat overcast given contrast with restraint), all reasoned to ONE house target read off the scene-lit grey concrete, so the naive move of auto-toning each clip or copying the hero's numbers visibly fails the match. On top sit an A/B thumbnail SET that must be two genuinely divergent authored art directions (loud warm-push vs teal cinematic duotone) from one frame, a frame-selection decision per clip (peak beat vs dead air), a brand-asset triage in OPPOSITE directions (vectorize the flat emblem via prep-before-trace; background-isolate the photoreal mascot — swapping them yields a black blob or a fuzzy screenshot), and three honest same-length reframes plus a speech enhance. The durable creative spine (six matched stills, A/B thumbnails, emblem SVG, mascot cut-out) is all [C] headless-confirmed so a grader can verify most of the deliverable autonomously; only the frame-pulls, reframes, summarize and speech-enhance are [A] async product-doable.
